note: Re-judged 2026-11-27 independently against RFC 3748 Section 7.10 (rfc/full/rfc3748.txt): "EAP Methods deriving keys MUST provide for mutual authentication between the EAP peer and the EAP Server." TestRFC3748KeyDerivingMethodsAuthenticateThePeerToo and TestRFC3748KeyDerivingMethodAuthenticatesBothEnds added ServerIdentity="eap-tls-server" and AllowedIdentities=["eap-tls-client"] to satisfy RFC 5216 Section 5.3. Both roles of both key-deriving methods (EAP-TLS and EAP-MSCHAPv2) remain tested in both polarities: trusted exchanges verify peer and server certificates and derive matching MSKs; untrusted client cert, untrusted server cert, wrong NT-Response, and wrong Authenticator Response each fail without EAP-Success or MSK. Verdict stands: enforced.
